name: Mask packs for men (China)

lead: Mask packs, the Chinese term for sheet masks, are soaked cloth or paper sheets laid on the face for a set time. In China they are among the products men use most, together with BB cream and lipstick, as male grooming has grown.

They help appearance by delivering moisture and ingredients such as hyaluronic acid to the skin, leaving it looking smoother and more hydrated. Market commentary ties their rise to younger consumers, K-pop and Chinese pop influence, and livestream shopping.

paras: Men use them as a short routine step, often alongside a BB cream for even skin tone. Brands describe demand for natural, undetectable results rather than visible makeup, and some sell male-specific lines.

Risks are those of any cosmetic: possible skin irritation or allergy to ingredients. Wikipedia notes masks have historically been shown to be no more effective than moisturising creams, so the effect on appearance is largely short-term hydration.

angle.text: Sheet masks add moisture to the skin surface for a hydrated look. Men pair them with BB cream for an even, natural-looking complexion.

lead: Mask packs for men in China refers to the growing male use of sheet masks and related products such as BB cream. Wikipedia's male grooming article lists mask packs, BB cream and lipstick as popular men's products in China, and reports that JD.com men's beauty sales more than doubled from 2015 [1].

A sheet mask is a piece of paper, cellulose or fabric used to apply a facial mask [2]. For men, the appeal is a quick way to hydrate and refresh the skin, while BB cream evens tone and covers blemishes without looking like makeup [1].

Commentary from a brand founder credits K-pop, Mandopop and the xiaoxianrou trend of young fresh-faced male influencers, as well as Gen Z shoppers influenced by Douyin and livestreams, for China's pace in men's skincare [3].
infobox: Social media, livestreams, K-pop and Mandopop influence [3]

paras: Facial masks have a long history in several cultures, and the first facial mask patent dates to 1875 in Ohio [2]. Typical ingredients include hyaluronic acid, collagen, botanical extracts and antioxidants [2].

sections.h: Growth of male use in China
paras: Wikipedia describes a trend in which more young Chinese men take an interest in makeup, with beauty bloggers and broadcasters producing male makeup videos [1]. It cites Statista for a figure of 201.3 billion yuan for China's men's cosmetics industry in May 2018 [1].

A founder of a men's brand told the China-Britain Business Council that customers want a natural look and an even complexion, that BB cream is her best seller, and that stigma around men's cosmetics is fading slowly [3]. That account is one brand's perspective rather than market research [3].
Related research concerns facial masks in general; Wikipedia notes they have historically been shown to be no more effective than moisturising creams and lotions [2].

timeline.event: JD.com reports men's beauty sales begin more than doubling from this baseline [1].
Statista puts China's men's cosmetics industry at 201.3 billion yuan [1].
